Was unable to replicate exact behavior due to the "Center of Other Screen" Initial Position Type not being respected on my machine for whatever reason, however throwing in some print statements even on the primary screen can see some odd behavior:

```
func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	print(DisplayServer.window_get_mode())
	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("toggle_fullscreen"):
		print("Pressed")
		if DisplayServer.window_get_mode() == DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
			print("Set WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED")
			DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED)
		else:
			print("Set WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN")
			DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)
```

The mode switching is done by sending EWMH (Extended Window Manager Hints) to the Window Manager, that is, the mode switch needs to wait for Window Manager to complete before it takes effect, it is not done in real time. The server uses the following code to wait so that the mode appears to be effective immediately.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/0793c626d2e203c6db04656853f8088478181888/platform/linuxbsd/x11/display_server_x11.cpp#L2831-L2838

However, it should be noted that due to the lack of `_NET_WM_ACTION_MAXIMIZE_HORZ` / `_NET_WM_ACTION_MAXIMIZE_VERT` in full-screen mode, `window_is_maximize_allowed()` returns `false` in full-screen mode. So the server is not actually waiting.

The issue is only present if I start the program directly in fullscreen **and** on the secondary monitor. That's the 1. case above. Switching from fullscreen to windowed works in all other cases. The only thing in which 1. differs from 2., 3., and 4. is that minimum and maximum size is set:

```diff
< 		program specified minimum size: 64 by 64
< 		program specified maximum size: 32768 by 32768
```

From the code it looks like these sizes shouldn't be set in fullscreen mode at all:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/841596cae4ddf97d67dc253021347bc01863f00f/platform/linuxbsd/x11/display_server_x11.cpp#L2248-L2285

So why are they set when starting in fullscreen on the secondary monitor? 🤷‍♂

Just encountered the same issue with my project and stumbled upon this thread. 
Workaround: start the game windowed and only maximize after loading is done.

How strange, I have exactly the opposite issue of @emogames .
When starting the game in windowed mode, function calls such as 

`DisplayServer.window_set_mode(mode,0)` or
`DisplayServer.window_set_size(size,0)`

do absolutely nothing. However when the game is launched in Fullscreen or Exclusive Fullscreen, the calls work without problem, even after switching to windowed mode -__________-

I ran into the same problem with Godot 4 and after some digging I noticed the behavior comes from how the window mode is being changed.

When using `DisplayServer.window_set_mode()`, the change is applied directly to the **window**. However, Godot’s project settings and the rendering pipeline expect the mode to be managed at the **viewport** level. Because of that, when the project is configured to start in fullscreen, switching back to windowed mode only through `DisplayServer` doesn’t “stick” — it gets overridden by the viewport’s mode a few frames later.

What worked for me was changing the mode via the viewport instead of the display server, e.g.:

```gdscript
if get_viewport().mode == DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN:
    get_viewport().mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED
else:
    get_viewport().mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN
```

This way, the change aligns with how project settings and the viewport handle resolution and window modes (as described in the [Multiple Resolutions docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/multiple_resolutions.html) and demonstrated in the [demo project](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/gui/multiple_resolutions#multiple-resolutions-crash-course).

I can’t say for sure this is the definitive fix for everyone, but in my case it solved the issue where toggling from fullscreen to windowed.

This issue is reproducible in 4.5.1.stable.

For the record, `get_viewport().mode = DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED` behaves exactly the same as `DisplayServer.window_set_mode(DisplayServer.WINDOW_MODE_WINDOWED)` on my PC.

However, the issue is **not** reproducible in 4.6.dev5. Something definitely changed in 4.6 because another small issue where window jumped to the other monitor after switching away from fullscreen is also gone.

After some searching I found out that it was fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/111580. I can reproduce it before this change and not after it.
